title: APIs, HTTP & FastAPI
goal: Client-server, HTTP methods, status codes, headers aur JSON samjhoge; requests se API call karoge (API key, timeout, error handling ke saath); REST design seekhoge, aur FastAPI se apna API bana ke ML model ko endpoint ke peeche serve karoge.

lessons.title: API aur client-server: do software ki baatcheet
blocks: **API** (Application Programming Interface) = do software ke beech baat karne ka tareeka. Ek program dusre se kehta hai "yeh do" ya "yeh karo", aur jawab leta hai.

Restaurant mein tu kitchen mein nahi ghusta. **Waiter** ko order deta hai, woh kitchen se khaana laata hai. Tu = **client**, kitchen = **server**, waiter + menu = **API**. Menu batata hai kya maang sakte ho, aur kaise.

Zomato app restaurant se baat karta hai = API. Weather app weather data laata hai = API. Tera Python code Claude/OpenAI ko prompt bhejta hai = API. Aur jab tu apna ML model banayega, mobile app ya website use **tere API** se hi use karegi.
**HTTP** = internet pe client aur server ke baat karne ke **rules** (protocol). Har baat do hisson mein hoti hai: **request** (client bhejta hai) aur **response** (server lautata hai).
**URL** ke bhi hisse hote hain. Python ka `urllib.parse` (stdlib) URL ko tod ke dikhata hai:

from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs

url = "https://api.geep.in:8000/v1/products?category=cable&limit=5"
p = urlparse(url)
print(p.scheme)
print(p.netloc)
print(p.path)
print(parse_qs(p.query))
**Path** batata hai *kaunsi cheez* (resource). **Query** (`?` ke baad, `&` se alag) batata hai *kaise* (filter, page, limit).

Dhyan se dekh: **Idempotent** = ek hi request 10 baar bhejo, result wahi rahega. GET 10 baar = same data. POST 10 baar = 10 naye records! Isliye payment jaisi POST request ko retry karte waqt dhyan rakhte hain.
Common galti: data badalne ke liye GET use karna (jaise `GET /delete?id=5`). GET sirf padhne ke liye hai; browser/cache GET ko kabhi bhi dobara bhej sakte hain.

lessons.title: Status codes, headers aur JSON
blocks: Har response ke saath ek **status code** aata hai: 3 digit ka number jo batata hai kya hua. Pehla digit family batata hai.

200 OK
201 Created
401 Unauthorized
403 Forbidden
404 Not Found
500 Internal Server Error

IQ trap: **401 vs 403**. 401 = tumne pehchaan hi nahi batayi (token nahi/galat). 403 = pehchaan sahi hai, lekin is kaam ki permission nahi. Gate pass nahi = 401; gate pass hai par admin floor pe nahi ja sakte = 403.
**Headers** = request/response ke saath extra info, jaise lifafe ke upar likha pata. Body ke andar data, header pe uske baare mein info.
**JSON** (JavaScript Object Notation) = API ki common bhasha. Bilkul Python dict/list jaisa dikhta hai, lekin yeh ek **text** hai. Python ka `json` module (stdlib) dono taraf badalta hai:

import json

profile = {"name": "Akash", "age": 25, "ml": True, "skills": ["Python", "SQL"], "manager": None}
text = json.dumps(profile)
print(text)
print(type(text))
back = json.loads(text)
print(back["skills"][1], type(back))
Dhyan se dekh: JSON mein `True` → `true`, `None` → `null`, aur hamesha **double quotes**. Tuple JSON mein list ban jaata hai.
Asli API response zyadatar **nested** hota hai (dict ke andar list, list ke andar dict). Neeche ek ML prediction API ka response parse karte hain:

import json

raw = '''{"model": "churn-v2", "status": "ok",
 "predictions": [
   {"customer": "Sharma", "label": "stay", "score": 0.91},
   {"customer": "Gupta", "label": "leave", "score": 0.77},
   {"customer": "Verma", "label": "leave", "score": 0.64}
 ]}'''
data = json.loads(raw)
print(data["model"], len(data["predictions"]))
leaving = [p["customer"] for p in data["predictions"] if p["label"] == "leave"]
print(leaving)
print(round(max(p["score"] for p in data["predictions"]), 2))
Agar key na ho to `data["x"]` KeyError dega. API data pe bharosa mat karo; `.get()` default ke saath use karo. Aur kharab JSON pe `json.JSONDecodeError` aata hai:

import json

resp = json.loads('{"name": "Akash"}')
print(resp.get("city", "N/A"))
try:
    json.loads("{name: Akash}")
except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
    print("Bad JSON:", e.msg)

N/A
Bad JSON: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes
Common galti: JSON string ko dict samajh ke `text["name"]` likhna. Pehle `json.loads()` karo. Aur `json.dumps` mein Hindi text ke liye `ensure_ascii=False` do, warna `\u0905` jaisa dikhega.

lessons.title: requests library: API call, API key, timeout, error handling
blocks: Python mein API call karne ki sabse popular library `requests` hai (`pip install requests`). Yeh internet maangta hai, isliye in examples ka output yahan nahi diya; neeche likha hai kya aata hai.

import requests

response = requests.get("https://api.github.com/users/octocat", timeout=10)
print(response.status_code)          # 200
data = response.json()               # JSON text -> Python dict
print(data["name"], data["public_repos"])
Chalaoge to `200` aur octocat ka naam aur repos count aayega. `requests.get()` = GET request; `response.json()` = body ko dict mein badalta hai (andar `json.loads` hi hai).
**Query params** khud mat jodo, `params=` do. **POST** mein data `json=` se bhejo, requests khud JSON banata hai aur `Content-Type` header lagata hai.

import requests

r = requests.get("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts",
                 params={"userId": 1}, timeout=10)
print(r.url)        # ...posts?userId=1

new_post = {"title": "GEEP", "body": "Hello", "userId": 1}
r = requests.post("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts", json=new_post, timeout=10)
print(r.status_code)   # 201 Created

**API key** = API ka ID card. Paid APIs (OpenAI, Claude, weather) bina key ke `401` dete hain. Key **header** mein jaati hai, aur code mein kabhi likhi nahi jaati; environment variable (`.env` file) se aati hai.

import os
import requests

api_key = os.getenv("API_KEY")          # .env / environment se
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
           "Content-Type": "application/json"}
r = requests.get("https://api.example.com/data", headers=headers, timeout=30)
Security rule: `api_key = "sk-abc123"` code mein likh ke GitHub pe push kiya to koi bhi use kar lega aur bill tera aayega. `.env` ko `.gitignore` mein daalo.
**Timeout** = itne second se zyada wait mat karo. Bina timeout ke, server atak gaya to tera program hamesha ke liye latka rahega.
ATM pe card daala aur internet chala gaya. ATM crash nahi hota, "Please try again" dikhata hai. Yahi **error handling** hai: problem aaye to crash mat karo, sambhalo.

Server kabhi kabhi thodi der ke liye fail hota hai (503, 429 rate limit). Tab **retry with backoff** karte hain: har baar thoda zyada ruk ke dobara try. Neeche ek nakli (fake) server se logic samjho, internet ki zaroorat nahi:

try 1: 503
  1s ruk ke retry
try 2: 503
  2s ruk ke retry
try 3: 200
final: 200
Sirf 5xx, 429 aur timeout pe retry karo. 400/401/404 pe retry bekaar hai, request hi galat hai. Real code mein yahan `time.sleep(wait)` lagta hai.
Common galti: bare `requests.get(url)` bina `timeout` aur bina try/except. Code review mein yeh reject hota hai.

lessons.title: REST API design: achha API kaisa dikhta hai
blocks: **REST** = API design ka ek style. Idea simple hai: har cheez ek **resource** hai (product, order, user) jiska ek URL hai, aur kaam HTTP method batata hai. URL mein **noun**, method mein **verb**.
Nesting relation ke liye: `/customers/3/orders` (customer 3 ke orders).
Version URL mein: `/v1/predict`, taaki naya version purane clients ko na tode.
Sahi status code lautao, sirf 200 nahi. Error ka body bhi JSON: `{"detail": "Product not found"}`.
**Stateless**: har request apne aap mein poori hoti hai (token bhi har baar header mein). Server pichli request yaad nahi rakhta. Isliye ek server ki jagah 10 server laga ke load baant sakte ho.
Railway enquiry counter: har baar tujhe PNR batana padta hai, clerk yaad nahi rakhta tu pehle aaya tha. Isi wajah se koi bhi khaali counter tera kaam kar sakta hai.
Ek chhota in-memory REST jaisa router bana ke dekhte hain, taaki method + path → status ka logic dimaag mein baith jaaye (yeh sirf Python hai, server nahi):
FastAPI yahi sab kaam (path todna, id ko int banana, validation, status code) tere liye apne aap karta hai. Agle lesson mein dekhenge.
Common galti: har response pe 200 bhejna aur body mein `{"error": true}` likhna. Client (aur monitoring tools) status code dekhte hain; galti pe 4xx/5xx hi bhejo.

lessons.title: FastAPI basics: apna API banana
blocks: **FastAPI** = Python se API server banane ka modern framework. Model bana liya, lekin mobile app ya website use kaise karegi? API se. FastAPI aaj AI/ML APIs ka industry standard hai.
AI model = kitchen ka chef. FastAPI = restaurant ka counter, jahan order aata hai, check hota hai, aur khaana bahar jaata hai. Uvicorn = restaurant ki building jisme counter chalta hai.
**Automatic validation**: Pydantic se galat data apne aap reject (422).
**Automatic docs**: `/docs` pe Swagger UI apne aap, bina kuch likhe test kar sakte ho.

pip install fastapi uvicorn
uvicorn main:app --reload        # main = file, app = FastAPI object
Server chala ke browser mein `http://localhost:8000/health` khologe to `{"status":"running"}` dikhega, aur `http://localhost:8000/docs` pe poora interactive documentation.
**Path parameter** = URL ka hissa (`{}` mein). **Query parameter** = function ka baaki argument, URL mein `?` ke baad. Type hint (`int`, `bool`) dene se FastAPI khud convert aur check karta hai.
Rule: argument ka naam path ke `{}` mein hai to path parameter, warna query parameter. Default value di to optional, nahi di to required.
**Pydantic model** = request body ka exact structure. Galat data aaye (type galat, field missing, range ke bahar) to FastAPI tera function chalne se pehle hi `422` laut deta hai.
`{"name": "PVC", "rate": -5}` bhejoge to 422 aayega (`rate` 0 se bada hona chahiye). `response_model` output ko bhi filter karta hai, taaki password jaisi internal field galti se bahar na jaaye.
**async**: jab function kisi cheez ka **intezaar** karta hai (database, dusra API, LLM call), tab `async def` + `await` se server us beech dusri requests sambhal leta hai.

Common galti: `async def` ke andar blocking cheez (jaise `requests.get` ya `time.sleep`, ya bhaari model calculation) chalana. Yeh poore event loop ko rok deta hai. Blocking kaam ho to normal `def` likho; FastAPI use threadpool mein chala deta hai.

lessons.title: ML model ko API ke peeche serve karna
blocks: Asli kaam: model train ho gaya, ab duniya use kaise kare? **Model ko ek baar load karo, `/predict` endpoint banao, input Pydantic se validate karo, prediction JSON mein lautao.**

# serve.py
import joblib
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

app = FastAPI(title="Churn Model API", version="1.0")
model = joblib.load("churn_model.joblib")   # startup pe EK baar load

class Customer(BaseModel):
    orders_last_90d: int = Field(..., ge=0)
    avg_amount: float = Field(..., ge=0)
    days_since_last_order: int = Field(..., ge=0)

class Prediction(BaseModel):
    will_leave: bool
    probability: float
    model_version: str

@app.post("/v1/predict", response_model=Prediction)
def predict(c: Customer):
    X = [[c.orders_last_90d, c.avg_amount, c.days_since_last_order]]
    prob = float(model.predict_proba(X)[0][1])
    return Prediction(will_leave=prob >= 0.5, probability=round(prob, 3),
                      model_version="1.0")

Request bhejoge `{"orders_last_90d": 1, "avg_amount": 4000, "days_since_last_order": 75}` to jawab kuch aisa aayega: `{"will_leave": true, "probability": 0.81, "model_version": "1.0"}` (number model pe depend karega).

Dhyan se dekh: model **har request pe load mat karo**. Load karne mein second lagte hain; global variable ya startup (`lifespan`) mein ek baar load karo. `predict` normal `def` hai kyunki model calculation CPU ka kaam hai, intezaar nahi.
Input validation (Pydantic) = galat data model tak pahunchta hi nahi.
`/health` endpoint rakho, taaki load balancer check kar sake server zinda hai.
Version URL aur response mein (`/v1`, `model_version`), taaki naya model aaye to pata rahe kisne kya diya.
Har prediction log karo (input, output, time), baad mein model monitoring ke kaam aata hai.
Batch endpoint (list of inputs) se ek call mein kai predictions: tez aur sasta.
Client side se call kaise hoga (requests se):

import requests

payload = {"orders_last_90d": 1, "avg_amount": 4000, "days_since_last_order": 75}
r = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/v1/predict", json=payload, timeout=10)
print(r.status_code, r.json())
Server ke bina bhi test likh sakte ho FastAPI ke `TestClient` se. Yeh pytest mein chalta hai:

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from serve import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_predict_ok():
    r = client.post("/v1/predict", json={"orders_last_90d": 3, "avg_amount": 900, "days_since_last_order": 4})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 0 <= r.json()["probability"] <= 1

def test_predict_bad_input():
    r = client.post("/v1/predict", json={"orders_last_90d": -1})
    assert r.status_code == 422
Production mein: Docker image, Gunicorn ke andar Uvicorn workers, aage Nginx. Yeh stage 14 mein detail se karenge. Abhi itna yaad rakho: **model + FastAPI + Pydantic + /docs = ek ML microservice.**

Common galti: training aur serving mein features ka order ya preprocessing alag ho jaana (training mein scaling ki, serving mein bhool gaye). Preprocessing ko model ke saath ek pipeline mein save karo (stage 10 mein `Pipeline`).

teach.say: API matlab do software ki baatcheet. Tera app request bhejta hai, server response lautata hai. Jaise waiter order le jaata hai aur khaana laata hai.
Request mein method batata hai kaam kya hai. GET lena, POST banana, PUT/PATCH badalna, DELETE hatana.
Response ke saath status code aata hai. 2 se shuru to success, 4 se shuru to client ki galti, 5 se shuru to server ki galti.
Data JSON mein aata-jaata hai. Python mein json.loads se text dict banta hai, json.dumps se dict text.
requests se call karo, lekin hamesha timeout ke saath, aur API key header mein, environment se.
Network kabhi bhi fail ho sakta hai. Try except lagao, aur 5xx pe thoda ruk ke retry karo.
REST mein URL noun hota hai aur method verb. slash products pe GET list deta hai, POST naya banata hai.
FastAPI mein decorator se endpoint banta hai. Type hint do, baaki validation aur docs FastAPI khud karta hai.
Pydantic model input ka darwaza hai. Galat data aaya to 422, tera function chalega hi nahi.

teach.say: Aakhir mein ML model: ek baar load karo, slash predict endpoint banao, aur JSON mein prediction lautao. Bas, tera model ab duniya use kar sakti hai.

iq.q: API kya hai? Ek real example do.
iq.a: API do software ke beech baat karne ka contract hai: kaunsa URL, kaunsa method, kya input, kya output. Jaise mera Python code Claude/OpenAI API ko prompt POST karta hai aur JSON mein jawab leta hai, ya mobile app mere FastAPI `/predict` endpoint se prediction leti hai.

iq.q: GET aur POST mein farak? Idempotent ka matlab?
iq.a: GET data padhne ke liye, data URL/query mein, cache ho sakta hai, idempotent hai. POST naya resource banane ke liye, data body mein, idempotent nahi (10 baar bhejo to 10 records). Idempotent = same request kitni bhi baar bhejo, server ki state ek hi baar jitni badalti hai. PUT aur DELETE bhi idempotent hain.
PUT poore resource ko naye data se replace karta hai (saari fields bhejni padti hain). PATCH sirf di gayi fields update karta hai, jaise sirf `rate` badalna.

iq.q: Common status codes batao, aur 401 vs 403?
iq.a: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict, 422 validation fail, 429 rate limit, 500 server error, 503 unavailable. 401 = authentication fail (token nahi/galat); 403 = authenticated hai lekin permission nahi.

iq.q: REST API kya hota hai? Achhe REST design ke principles?
iq.a: REST ek architecture style hai jisme har cheez resource hai jiska URL hota hai, aur HTTP methods se uspe kaam hota hai. Principles: plural noun URLs (`/products/7`), sahi methods aur status codes, stateless requests, JSON responses, filter/pagination query params mein, aur versioning (`/v1`).

iq.q: External API call ko production-ready kaise banaoge?
iq.a: Har call pe timeout, try/except (Timeout, ConnectionError, HTTPError), `raise_for_status()`, 5xx/429 pe exponential backoff ke saath limited retries, API key environment se, aur logging. Response ko `.get()` se padhna taaki missing keys pe crash na ho.

iq.q: FastAPI kyun? Flask/Django se kaise alag?
iq.a: FastAPI API-first framework hai: type hints se automatic validation (Pydantic), automatic Swagger docs `/docs` pe, aur native async support (ASGI). Flask minimal hai, sab khud jodna padta hai. Django full-stack hai, ORM aur admin built-in, bade web apps ke liye. ML model serving ke liye FastAPI sabse common hai.

iq.q: Path parameter aur query parameter mein farak?
iq.a: Path parameter URL ka hissa hai aur resource identify karta hai: `/products/{id}`. Query parameter `?` ke baad aata hai aur filter/sort/pagination ke liye hota hai: `/products?category=cable&limit=10`. FastAPI mein jo argument path ke `{}` mein hai woh path param, baaki query param.

iq.q: Pydantic kya karta hai, aur response_model kyun use karte ho?
iq.a: Pydantic request data ko types aur rules (`Field(gt=0)`, `min_length`) ke hisaab se validate aur convert karta hai; galat pe FastAPI 422 deta hai. `response_model` output ka structure fix karta hai, docs mein dikhata hai, aur extra fields (jaise password hash) filter kar deta hai taaki leak na ho.

iq.q: async def kab use karoge aur kab nahi?
iq.a: Jab endpoint I/O ka intezaar karta hai (database, dusra API, LLM call) aur us library ka async version hai (httpx, asyncpg), tab `async def` + `await`. CPU-heavy kaam (model inference, image processing) ya blocking library ho to normal `def`, kyunki async ke andar blocking call poore event loop ko rok deti hai; FastAPI `def` ko threadpool mein chalata hai.

iq.q: Ek trained ML model ko API ke roop mein kaise deploy karoge?
iq.a: Model ko joblib/pickle (ya ONNX) mein save karo, FastAPI app mein startup pe ek baar load karo, Pydantic se input schema banao, `/v1/predict` POST endpoint banao jo prediction aur model version JSON mein lautaye, `/health` endpoint rakho. Phir TestClient se tests, Docker image, Uvicorn/Gunicorn workers aur Nginx ke peeche deploy, aur predictions log karke monitoring.

Browser ka security rule: ek origin (domain+port) ka JavaScript dusre origin pe request tabhi bhej sakta hai jab server allow kare. Jaise React frontend port 5173 pe aur FastAPI 8000 pe, toh backend mein `CORSMiddleware` se allowed origins batane padte hain. Yeh sirf browser pe lagta hai, Python requests pe nahi.
